anchors.name: a1-descent
anchors.note: The establishing frame, looking back at the way in. Tests the shaft as the only "up", the rubble spill, and whether the hand-cut vault reads under a single cold source plus headlamp.

anchors.name: a2-shaft
anchors.note: Up into the break-in from beside the spill. Tests the broken floor slab, snapped joists, rim stones and the lit dust — the one moment the room admits there is a building above it.

anchors.name: a3-names
anchors.note: THE scene. Square on the east wall from 2.55 m — the far side of the chamber, because the headlamp is an inverse-square 900 and anything inside ~2 m clips to white. Tests inscription legibility, the carve normal and block-face relief. If the names cannot be read here, nothing else matters.

anchors.name: a4-niche
anchors.note: A punishment niche at 1.6 m: iron staple, tally marks, segmental head, 0.85 m deep. Tests the arch geometry and that the recess reads as a place a person was put, not a decorative alcove.

anchors.name: a5-seal
anchors.note: The brick seal at the far end over standing water, with the sodium bleed from the ventilator flue on the right. Tests brick-vs-limestone contrast, the water clear coat, the warm/cool split at depth, and the payload: someone did this deliberately.
